questions.q: How do you start building a join (rather than a relationship) between two tables in Tableau?
options: Drag or double-click the second table onto an existing logical table, which opens the physical layer and starts a join
Drag the second table next to the first on the logical layer canvas
Right-click the worksheet and select Insert Join
Joins can only be created in Tableau Prep, never in Desktop
questions.explain: Dragging a table next to another creates a relationship on the logical layer. Dragging or double-clicking a table onto an existing logical table opens its physical layer and starts a join.

questions.q: How do you add a second matching field pair to a join — Tableau's equivalent of a composite-key ON clause?
options: Click 'Add new join clause' in the Join dialog and pick a second field pair
You can't join on more than one field in Tableau
Create two separate joins and union the results
Edit the underlying SQL query directly in a text box
questions.explain: Each 'Add new join clause' entry is one more matching condition — functionally equivalent to one more AND in a SQL ON clause.

questions.q: In SQL terms, what does adding two join clauses to one Tableau join behave like?
options: ON a.Col1 = b.Col1 AND a.Col2 = b.Col2 — a row must satisfy every clause to match
ON a.Col1 = b.Col1 OR a.Col2 = b.Col2 — a row matches if either clause is true
Two separate joins run independently and then unioned
It has no SQL equivalent — it's a Tableau-only concept
questions.explain: Multiple join clauses in Tableau are combined with AND logic, just like stacking multiple conditions in a SQL ON clause — every clause must be satisfied for a row to match.

questions.q: Which Tableau join type keeps every row from the second (right-hand) table regardless of a match, matching SQL's RIGHT JOIN?
options: Right
Left
Inner
Full Outer only
questions.explain: Tableau's Right join type is the exact equivalent of SQL's RIGHT JOIN — every row from the second table is kept whether or not it matches.

questions.q: How do you remove a join clause you added by mistake?
options: Hover over the right side of the join clause and click the 'x' that appears
Delete the entire data source and start over
Join clauses can't be removed once added
Switch the join type to Full Outer, which clears all clauses
questions.explain: Hovering over a join clause reveals an 'x' on its right side — clicking it removes just that clause, leaving the rest of the join intact.
